issues.legal_issue: Different compensation and review rules for landowners whose land is compulsorily acquired for a local authority violate equal protection when the acquiring authority is the government and the distinctions do not rest on a relevant classification.
material_facts: Land was compulsorily acquired by the Collector for a municipal authority and then transferred to that authority.

The challenged modifications excluded potential value from compensation, restricted access to compensation review unless security for costs was deposited, and initially excluded solatium for certain acquisitions.
Under the unmodified acquisition law, similarly situated landowners could receive more compensation and seek review without the challenged security requirement.
The government could acquire land for the same public purpose under either the unmodified law or the modified rules, resulting in different treatment of landowners.
issues.conclusion: The challenged modifications discriminated between similarly situated landowners and violated Article 14; the modifications were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits legislative classification only when it is based on an intelligible differentia that has a rational nexus with the legislative object. Different compensation or review rules cannot ordinarily be justified merely because land is acquired for a particular public purpose or under a different acquisition regime when the acquiring authority is the government and affected owners are similarly situated. The Court followed Nagpur Improvement Trust v. Vithal Rao, [1973] 1 SCC 500. The Court also relied on sections 16, 17-A and 376, Schedule II, and section 372(1) of the U.P. Nagar Mahapalika Adhiniyam, 1959, in determining the acquiring authority and the effect of the challenged rules.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_acquisition_rules and government_acquires_for_local_authority and landowners_are_similarly_situated and modified_rules_reduce_compensation_or_review_rights and treatment_differs_without_relevant_classification

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_acquisition_: A party challenges the constitutionality of rules governing compulsory acquisition.
predicates.government_acquires_for_local_authority: The government compulsorily acquires land for a local authority and transfers the land to that authority.
predicates.landowners_are_similarly_situated: The affected landowners are similarly situated in relation to the acquisition.
predicates.modified_rules_reduce_compensation_or_re: The rules applied to the acquisition reduce compensation or restrict the landowners' ability to obtain review of the award.
predicates.treatment_differs_without_relevant_class: Landowners receive different treatment despite no relevant distinction that justifies the difference.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns acquisition rules that reduce compensation or review rights for similarly situated landowners without a relevant basis for different treatment, those rules are invalid for unequal treatment.

issues.legal_issue: Repeal of a restriction on receiving solatium applies to a compensation reference that remains pending when the restriction is repealed, absent a saving of pending proceedings.
material_facts: A restriction had been added to the compensation law that excluded solatium for certain acquisitions.
The restriction was repealed while the landowners' compensation claim remained pending before the Tribunal.
The repealing law contained no provision saving pending references from the repeal.
issues.conclusion: The Tribunal had to treat the repealed restriction as though it had never existed and could not deny solatium on the basis of that restriction.
issues.legal_principle: The repeal was final and unconditional, and no saving provision preserved the restriction for pending references. Because compensation remained under consideration, the Tribunal had to give effect to the repeal. The Court considered the restriction on solatium under section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as modified and subsequently repealed by the U.P. Amendment Act 23 of 1961.

predicates.pending_compensation_reference: A claimant's compensation reference remains undecided when the relevant legal change occurs.
predicates.restriction_on_compensation_repealed: A restriction that limited the claimant's entitlement to compensation is repealed.
predicates.repeal_has_no_saving_for_pending_claims: The repealing law does not preserve the restriction for claims that are still pending.

issues.definition: If a compensation reference is pending when a restriction is repealed without saving pending claims, the claim is decided without that restriction.

issues.legal_issue: A scheme carried forward from a repealed enactment is subject to the new enactment's completion time limit, which runs from the date the scheme is deemed notified under the new enactment.
material_facts: The housing scheme had been notified under the earlier enactment before that enactment was repealed.
The new enactment provided for continuation of earlier schemes and proceedings, deeming a carried-forward scheme to have been notified under the new enactment.
The land acquisition award was made within five years of the new enactment coming into force.
issues.conclusion: The new enactment's five-year completion limit applied to the carried-forward scheme, with the period commencing when the scheme was deemed notified under the new enactment; the award was within that period, so the scheme had not lapsed for failure to meet the time limit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 365(4) of the U.P. Nagar Mahapalika Adhiniyam, 1959, imposed a time limit for completing acquisition through the award stage. Section 577(a) had to be read with sections 577(b) and 577(c), including their legal fiction that earlier schemes and acquisition proceedings continued as if under the new enactment. This reading avoided an unreasonable result in which new schemes were time-limited but older carried-forward schemes could continue indefinitely.

rule.if: challenge_to_continuing_acquisition_scheme and scheme_carried_forward_under_new_law and scheme_deemed_notified_when_new_law_began and award_made_within_completion_period

predicates.challenge_to_continuing_acquisition_sche: A party contends that a continuing land-acquisition scheme has lapsed for failure to meet a completion time limit.
predicates.scheme_carried_forward_under_new_law: A scheme begun under an earlier legal regime continues under a later legal regime.
predicates.scheme_deemed_notified_when_new_law_bega: The later legal regime treats the carried-forward scheme as notified when that regime began.
predicates.award_made_within_completion_period: The acquisition award is made within the applicable completion period measured from the deemed notification.

issues.definition: A carried-forward scheme does not lapse for missing its completion limit when the award is made within the period measured from the date it is deemed notified under the new legal regime.
